nodes.name: NiFe-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The NiFe-LDH was fabricated employing a similar strategy without adding the F source.
nodes.source_text: For comparison, the NiFe-LDH was also fabricated employing a similar strategy without adding the F source.

nodes.name: F-NiFe-LDH-X hydrothermal fluorination
nodes.procedure: F-NiFe-LDH-Xs (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10) with different fluorination degrees were constructed via a facile one-step hydrothermal method by adjusting NaF feeding (1, 3, 5, and 10 mmol), which is expected to promote OER and inhibit chloride corrosion. The F atoms could easily enter into the lattices of NiFe-LDH by isomorphous substitution, due to their similar atomic sizes for F and O.
nodes.source_text: F-NiFe-LDH-Xs (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10) with different fluorination degrees were constructed via a facile one-step hydrothermal method by adjusting NaF feeding, e.g., 1, 3, 5, and 10 mmol, which is expected to promote OER and inhibit chloride corrosion (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: by adjusting NaF feeding, e.g., 1, 3, 5, and 10 mmol

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal treatment

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: The OER performance of the F-NiFe-LDH was assessed in alkaline simulated seawater... at 200 mA cm^{-2} it needs an overpotential of merely 287 mV... 500 and even 800 mA cm^{-2} the lowest overpotentials of 306 and 334 mV... Tafel slope of F-NiFe-LDH is 39.1 mV dec^{-1}... mass activities, with 440 and 1472 A g_{cat}^{-1} at... 300 and 400 mV... TOF of 0.84 s^{-1} @ η_{400}... The F-NiFe-LDH exhibits a much lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct)

nodes.description: OER performance in alkaline seawater (1.0 M KOH + seawater)
nodes.source_text: the F-NiFe-LDH exhibits a superior oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity with low overpotentials of 306 and 375 mV to reach 500 mA cm^{-2} at alkaline simulated seawater and alkaline seawater, respectively.

nodes.description: Stability testing at 500 mA/cm2 in alkaline simulated seawater
nodes.source_text: In alkaline simulated seawater, the F-NiFe-LDH presents ultra-stability after 150 h of electrolysis at 500 mA cm^{-2}, as evidenced by negligible performance degradation

nodes.description: Long-term stability at 1000 mA/cm2 in alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: it demonstrates... ultra-stability seawater electrolysis for over 1000 h at 1000 mA cm^{-2} without performance degradation... achieves sustained electrolysis of alkaline seawater (1.0 M KOH + seawater) over 1000 h under industrial-level current density without any structural degradation

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer stability at 500 mA/cm2 in alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: the F-NiFe-LDH || Pt electrolyzer can drive 500 mA cm^{-2} of electrolysis at only 2.04 V cell voltage... energy consumption (EC) is only 4.87 kWh Nm^{-3} H2... the electrolyzer sustains for 80 h without obvious degradation at 500 mA cm^{-2}

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency measurement for seawater electrolysis
nodes.source_text: The Faradaic efficiency (FE) for seawater electrolysis, ascertained through the drainage method... shows that the molar amounts of H2 and O2 produced over electrolysis time are always in good agreement with the theoretical 2:1 ratio, meaning that the FE approaches 100%

nodes.description: pH dependence OER testing in various KOH electrolytes
nodes.source_text: with an increase in pH from 12.73 to 14.01, the OER activity of F-NiFe-LDH enhanced significantly

nodes.description: Kinetic isotope effect testing in NaOH vs NaOD
nodes.source_text: the use of the isotope D causes a severe degradation in the activity of F-NiFe-LDH. Moreover, the kinetic isotope effect (KIE) is ascertained through the ratio of current densities in NaOH (jH) to NaOD (jD)... the value of jH/jD for F-NiFe-LDH is consistently higher

nodes.characterization_summary: F-NiFe-LDH-Xs (X = 1, 3, and 5) show vertically oriented nanosheet morphology grown on nickel foam, similar to NiFe-LDH; F-NiFe-LDH-10 shows nanosheet agglomeration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The changes in the morphology of the as-prepared catalysts with fluorination degree were demonstrated through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images. The F-NiFe-LDH-Xs (X = 1, 3, and 5) show the vertically oriented nanosheet morphology grown on nickel foam (NF), similar to NiFe-LDH (Figure S3, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows Ni³⁺ (857.4/875.5 eV) and Ni²⁺ (855.8/873.9 eV) peaks; Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio increases with fluorination, maximum in F-NiFe-LDH-5; F 1s peak at 684.2 eV confirms M-F bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni²⁺ (855.8/873.9 eV) and Ni³⁺ (at 857.4/875.5 eV) together with two satellite peaks can be identified in Figure 2c... the peaks at around 684.2 eV are consistent with the M-F bonds in F-NiFeLDH-X samples (X = 1,3, and 5)

properties.title: Long-term stability at high current densities

properties.description: Fluorine-doped Nickel-Iron Layered Double Hydroxide with 5% doping

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks at 475 cm⁻¹ (Ni²⁺-O) and 553 cm⁻¹ (Ni³⁺-O); F-NiFe-LDH-5 shows higher I₅₅₃/I₄₇₅ ratios and reconstruction hysteresis at 1.40 V vs RHE vs 1.35 V for NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From in situ Raman spectra in Figure 2e,f, the characteristic peaks at 475 and 553 cm⁻¹, correspond to Ni³⁺-O in reconstruction product NiOOH... the values of I₅₅₃/I₄₇₅ for F-NiFe-LDH-5, which are consistently higher than those of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Low loading shows no evident diffraction peaks except NF; catalyst powders confirm NiFe-LDH phase for both samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Because of low loading mass, no evident diffraction peaks are detected via the X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectrum except the NF (Figure S9a, Supporting Information). Furthermore, the catalyst powders were investigated by XRD and both were proved to be NiFe-LDH phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes show 0.197 nm spacing matching (018) plane of NiFe-LDH; F modification results in large amorphous regions and significant lattice distortions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM images (Figure 3a,b) reveal an average spacing of 0.197 nm between lattice fringes, matching with the (018) plane for NiFe-LDH. Notably, the modification of F results in the appearance of large amorphous regions, along with significant lattice distortions.

nodes.characterization_summary: F element is uniformly substituted throughout F-NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element of F is uniformly substituted throughout the F-NiFe-LDH, as demonstrated by energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) (Figure S12, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 3420, 1628 cm⁻¹ (interlayer water) and 1352 cm⁻¹ (interlayer CO₃²⁻) confirm layered double hydroxide structure preserved after F substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As detected from Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra, the peaks centered at 3420 and 1628 cm⁻¹ are attributed to interlayer water, while the peak at 1352 cm⁻¹ is associated with interlayer CO₃²⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic signal at g = 2.007 indicates unpaired electrons in lattice oxygen; F-NiFe-LDH shows significantly higher signal intensity than NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron spin resonance (ESR) measurements were carried out to identify the O_v. Figure S14 (Supporting Information) shows the characteristic signals at g = 2.007 indicative of unpaired electrons in lattice oxygen.

nodes.characterization_summary: F-NiFe-LDH exhibits prominent peak at 600-700°C for strong Lewis acid sites; NiFe-LDH shows more medium acid sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c shows that the curves can be distinguished into three acidity regions... The F-NiFe-LDH exhibits a prominent peak in the range of 600 - 700°C, attributing to strong Lewis acid sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Et₃PO chemical shift shifts from 49.8 ppm (free) to 49.9 ppm (NiFe-LDH) and 51.6 ppm (F-NiFe-LDH), indicating harder Lewis acidity in F-NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3d, the ³¹P chemical shift of Et₃PO is 49.8 ppm. Upon binding to NiFe-LDH, the peak shifts slightly to 49.9 ppm. In contrast, the peak of Et₃PO-bound F-NiFe-LDH significantly shifts to a much lower field at 51.6 ppm.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 150 h chronopotentiometry at 500 mA cm⁻², F-NiFe-LDH maintains uniform structure covering NF; NiFe-LDH shows only partial residues with severe pitting corrosion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the F-NiFe-LDH still maintains an ultra-stable structure and covers the NF uniformly... while there are only partial catalyst residues over NF for NiFe-LDH accompanied by severe pitting corrosion (Figure 6d,e).
